title: the Glass Steppe Rising Anew
premise: Isandro Zhou keeps the ledgers of the Glass Steppe, a guild that trades in impossible things, and guards a gate that should stay shut — until the crown's hunt for the gifted drives refugees to their door. When Isandro discovers the king has been hollowed out and replaced by something wearing his crown, they must choose between the guild's neutrality and justice that exists outside any law. Gathering a fugitive archivist, a disgraced royal huntsman, and the last free-city smugglers, Isandro races to unbind the true king before the usurper's armies swallow the free cities. In the end, Isandro unbinds the king at the cost of sealing the gate forever — and of the ledger-name that made them who they were.
about_author: August Zhou is the pen name of a former customs clerk who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated goods in a border city, an experience that taught them how much contraband can look like hope. They write fantasy about people who keep records of things the powerful would rather forget.

chapters.title: The Weight of Entries
chapters.summary: Isandro Zhou, POV. Isandro audits the guild's ledgers at the Glass Steppe, noting impossible trades: bottled storms, borrowed years, a door sold twice. The chapter establishes their meticulous identity as keeper of both books and gate, and ends when a bloodied stranger arrives carrying a page torn from Isandro's own ledger — one Isandro never wrote. Beat: quiet dread beneath routine.

chapters.title: What the Crown Proclaims
chapters.summary: Maren Voss, a royal archivist, POV. In the capital, Maren copies the proclamation of the Gift Hunt — every gifted person to be registered, then rendered. She recognizes the decree's language as older than the dynasty, sourced from sealed archives she alone can read. Fearing what it means, she flees with stolen folios. Beat: conscience over career.

chapters.title: Refugees at the Gate
chapters.summary: Isandro, POV. Gifted families arrive at the Steppe seeking passage through the shut gate; guild law forbids opening it. Isandro secretly logs them anyway, hiding names inside trade entries. The torn ledger page proves to be a prophecy written in Isandro's own hand — dated three years from now. Beat: compassion against rules.

chapters.title: The Huntsman's Oath
chapters.summary: Dain Corvale, POV. Dain, the crown's finest huntsman, captures a gifted child and watches his superiors 'render' her into a pale, obedient thing. He realizes the Hunt isn't containment but harvest. He burns his warrant and rides for the free cities, hunted by his own former company. Beat: disillusionment turned to defection.

chapters.title: Ledger of the Impossible
chapters.summary: Isandro, POV. Maren arrives seeking asylum and deciphers the false entry: it predicts the gate will open on a specific night, and names Isandro as its opener. The guild council votes to expel all gifted refugees to appease the crown. Isandro falsifies the expulsion record — their first crime. Beat: identity cracking open.

chapters.title: Salt Roads
chapters.summary: Dain, POV. Wounded and pursued, Dain stumbles onto a smuggler caravan bound for the Steppe, led by the irreverent captain Sefa Ilun. He bargains his knowledge of the Hunt's routes for passage. Along the salt roads he sees villages emptied, their gifted taken. Beat: guilt sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Council of Weights
chapters.summary: Isandro, POV. The guild masters confront Isandro about the forged entry; neutrality is the Steppe's only survival. Isandro argues some things cannot be weighed. That night, the usurper's envoy offers gold for the refugees and Isandro's head. The council wavers. Beat: isolation of principle.

chapters.title: A Door Sold Twice
chapters.summary: Maren, POV. Maren studies the stolen folios and finds the truth: generations ago, a court sorcerer bound himself to the royal line, and each heir has been slowly consumed. The current king is nearly gone; the thing wearing the crown now writes decrees in his stead. Beat: horror of discovery, resolve forming.

chapters.title: Night of Knives
chapters.summary: Isandro, POV. Assassins strike the Steppe to seize the ledger and the refugees. Isandro, Maren, and the refugees fight through the archive halls; the guild master dies shielding the books, whispering that the gate was never meant to keep things out — but to keep one thing in. Beat: grief and betrayal.

chapters.title: Flight Across the Steppe
chapters.summary: Dain, POV. Dain's caravan meets the fleeing Steppe survivors on the open grassland. He and Isandro recognize each other across old enmities — he once raided a Steppe waystation. Sefa brokers uneasy alliance. Together they outrun the first columns of the usurper's army. Beat: enemies becoming comrades.

chapters.title: The Free Cities Hear
chapters.summary: Maren, POV. In the free city of Vhalen, the refugees plead their case before a merchant council too cowardly to act. Maren publicly reads the binding-ritual evidence; riots spark; the council disavows them. But word spreads, and volunteers gather — smiths, deserters, gifted children. Beat: despair seeding defiance.

chapters.title: What Isandro Carries
chapters.summary: Isandro, POV. Interlude of memory: Isandro's childhood as a foundling raised by the guild, the day they first opened the gate's antechamber and heard something breathing behind it, and why they've never spoken of it. The prophecy entry makes terrible sense now. Beat: intimate reckoning with self.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Court
chapters.summary: Dain, POV. Captured scouts reveal the usurper's plan: after conquering the free cities, the crown-thing will feed ten thousand gifted souls to the binding and become unkillable. Dain recognizes his old commander among the officers and realizes the Hunt was designed by someone who knew the ritual. Beat: stakes made flesh.

chapters.title: Bargains in Bone and Ink
chapters.summary: Isandro, POV. To learn how to unbind a king, Isandro trades with the Steppe's most dangerous client: a lich-broker who deals in memories. The price is Isandro's ledger-name — the recorded identity that anchors their gift. Isandro pays, feeling part of themselves go quiet. Beat: sacrifice without certainty.

chapters.title: The Army at the River
chapters.summary: Sefa Ilun, POV. The usurper's vanguard reaches the river before Vhalen. Sefa's smugglers burn the bridges and run munitions lines while Maren evacuates civilians. The free cities' ragged defense holds for three days. Sefa loses her ship and half her crew. Beat: costly courage.

chapters.title: Into the Antechamber
chapters.summary: Isandro, POV. Guided by the prophecy entry, Isandro opens the gate at last — inward. Behind it lies the antechamber where the original sorcerer's binding is anchored, and the breathing thing: the first king, still half-alive, still bound. It shows Isandro the unbinding rite and warns what it will cost. Beat: awe and terror.

chapters.title: The Fall of Vhalen
chapters.summary: Maren, POV. Vhalen's walls break. Maren stays behind to destroy the archive rather than let the crown-thing claim the ritual texts, and is captured. Through her eyes we see the usurper up close: the king's body moving like a puppet, the crown drinking light. Beat: darkest hour.

chapters.title: Ride of the Broken Company
chapters.summary: Dain, POV. Dain leads a desperate strike to extract Maren from the occupying camp, joined by defecting huntsmen who followed him after all. They succeed barely; Dain faces his old commander and refuses to kill him, breaking the cycle. Beat: redemption chosen over vengeance.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Isandro, POV. At the gate, Isandro performs the rite with Maren's recovered fragments and Dain holding the threshold. The binding tears loose; the crown-thing, severed from its anchor across the kingdom, begins to unravel. The true king wakes far away in his own body, old and weeping. Beat: climax, triumph shadowed by cost.

chapters.title: What the Gate Keeps Now
chapters.summary: Isandro, POV. The unraveling crown-thing hurls itself at the gate to re-anchor through it. Isandro chooses to seal the gate permanently from within the antechamber — the role the prophecy always named. Dain and Maren pull them back at the final second; the first king takes Isandro's place willingly, ending his long captivity. Beat: fate rewritten by choice.

chapters.title: Ledgers Closed, Ledgers Opened
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided. The armies dissolve as the binding fails; the true king, restored but frail, abolishes the Hunt and grants the free cities charter. Isandro, nameless now, begins a new ledger with a blank first page — and writes their own name in it, choosing who they are. Beat: rebirth.

chapters.title: The Glass Steppe Rising Anew
chapters.summary: Isandro, POV, epilogue. A year later, the Steppe reopens as a school and sanctuary where the gifted are taught rather than traded. Maren curates honest archives; Dain trains wardens who answer to no crown; Sefa sails again. Isandro locks the dead gate's door one last time and walks out into the grass. Beat: peace earned, identity self-made.
